text:
sam: Heads-up — saw a latency regression on hybrid quant (FP8+INT4) after the scheduler change this morning. Microbenching shows weird tail latencies when continuous-batcher packs small sequences into large kernels.

marta: OK can you paste the numbers? is this on dedicated or hosted?

sam: Hosted, perf cluster in us-west. Quick numbers from bench run: 
```
model: gpt-7b-hybrid
quant: hybrid4fp8
batcher: continuous
shapes sampled: [1,4,8,16,32,64]
throughput baseline (master before scheduler change): 12.4k tok/s
throughput current: 9.7k tok/s
p50 p99 latency baseline: 45ms / 210ms
p50 p99 current: 50ms / 620ms
tail explodes when >45% of incoming shapes are length<=8
```

kevin: Oof. That p99 jump smells like padding blowup + kernel fallback thrash. Did the selector start preferring an FP8 kernel that can't handle small shapes efficiently?

sam: Yeah, selector logs show it picked `fp8-kernel-multiwarp-v3` for many batches because of new cost model. But that kernel assumes a packed tile width of 64; when we pack a bunch of len<=8 requests we end up with extreme internal padding and KV-cache alignments that balloon memory ops.

jia: Can you share the selector trace? also any perf-bot snapshots?

sam: Pasted trace below (trimmed):
```
[selector] candidate kernels: [int4-pack-v2(cost=1.2), fp8-kernel-multiwarp-v3(cost=0.9), fp8-slab(cost=1.1)]
[selector] chosen: fp8-kernel-multiwarp-v3
[batcher] inbound shapes: [1,1,4,8,8,16,32,64,1,4]
[batcher] packed shape -> kernel shape: 64x1024 (lots of pad)
[kvcache] alignment_shifts: [0,56,56,56,...]
[runtime] mmcopy time increased by ~3.8x vs baseline
```

marta: That alignment_shifts line is telling — we probably mis-estimated the cost of memcpy when pad ratio > 0.6. New scheduler cost model weights memcpy lower which now biases toward large-kernel FP8 paths.

kevin: Quick mitigation: add a heuristic in the batcher to prefer kernels with pack_width <= median_request_len*4 when tail pad ratio > 0.5. Short-term we can also force `int4-pack-v2` for those traffic slices.

jia: If we force int4, quality might dip for some prompts. Do we have eval buckets showing quality delta?

sam: Small eval run shows negligible quality delta for system prompts (loss +0.02) but some safety prompts show token choice drift. We should A/B for a day.

perf-bot: snapshot attached (run:1958765401): high memcpy stall on GPU0, kernel occupancy reduced due to warp fragmentation.

marta: Can someone reproduce locally with the microbench script? Use these flags: 
```
./bench --model gpt-7b --batcher continuous --quant hybrid4fp8 --max-len 512 --shape-dist "heavy-short" --runs 50
```

kevin: I'll run it on my dev node now. Quick idea for selector change: include an estimated pad_mem_cost term = pad_tokens * mem_per_token / mem_bandwidth and penalize kernels where pad_mem_cost > threshold. That should push the cost model away from huge-pad kernels for skewed shapes.

sam: Agree. Also, KV-cache behavior: when we split packs across slabs the KV read pattern causes multiple small memcpy ops rather than one big read because of slab boundaries. We should add a slab-coalescing pass in the packer.

jia: Great call. Two action items: (1) kevin adds pad_mem_cost heuristic + short-circuit rule to pick int4 for heavy-short traffic; (2) eng-runtime implements slab coalescing in packer and we run end-to-end bench. I'll open a canary rollout for the int4 short-term fix.

kevin: On it — will push a prototype PR and include microbench numbers. ETA a few hours.

sam: Thanks — saving the profiler traces to the incident bucket: s3://redwood-perf/1958765432/ — tags: hybrid-quant, continuous-batcher, kv-slab.

marta: Nice. If we can't get the allocator/packer fix quickly, consider lowering the continuous-batcher max_pack_width for hosted-tier to 32 as a stopgap.

perf-bot: alert cleared after throttle applied at 1958765488 (rate-limit on continuous pack width).

kevin: PR up: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2345 — includes pad_mem_cost + option `prefer_int4_on_short_skew`. Microbench numbers in PR description show p99 back to ~220ms.

sam: Verified on us-west mirror — p99 drops to 230ms, throughput ~11.9k tok/s. Leaving canary running for 6h.

marta: Perfect. Follow-up: let's add a unit test for slab coalescing and a selector sim test with synthetic shape distributions. Also add telemetry: report tail_pad_ratio and chosen_kernel per batch in tracing.

jia: I'll add the tracing fields. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: Closing thread once canary done.
